tiers.name: Severely Deprived (Acute Homelessness)
tiers.living: Sleeping rough, cars or tents, emergency shelters, motels, women's refuges, or severely overcrowded couch surfing.
tiers.character: No legal right to stay, little privacy or control, or lacking basic amenities. Needs immediate crisis intervention, such as Housing First.

tiers.name: Unstable / Transitional
tiers.living: Transitional housing, short-term boarding houses, campgrounds, or a temporary stay with family or whānau.
tiers.character: A roof, but time-limited and without long-term security of tenure. Wrap-around support is aimed at a permanent home.

tiers.name: At Risk (Housing Insecure)
tiers.living: Private rental or mortgaged home under severe financial stress, overcrowding, or poor physical conditions.
tiers.character: Often more than 30–50% of income on housing, with arrears, eviction pressure, or a cold or damp home. Prevention support is the relevant response.

tiers.name: Subsidised / Assisted Stability
tiers.living: Public or social housing, community housing, rent-to-buy, or shared equity.
tiers.character: Longer security of tenure, with a government or non-profit subsidy such as income-related rent keeping the cost workable.

tiers.name: Stable / Market Secure
tiers.living: Unsubsidised homeownership, or a long-term private rental the household can afford.
tiers.character: Security of tenure, a habitable dwelling, and housing costs that are sustainable against income.
